title: OmniQEC: discovering practical quantum error-correcting codes by an AI scientist
authors: Ge Yan, Shanchuan Li, Pengyue Ma, Qixin Zhang, Pingchuan Ma, Jianping Wang, Min-Hsiu Hsieh, Yuxuan Du
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is indispensable for scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing. However, discovering QEC codes that remain effective is challenging, as logical performance depends on the interplay between code structure, hardware, syndrome extraction, and decoding, which often impose competing requirements. Here we introduce OmniQEC, an efficient AI scientist for discovering QEC codes suited to deployment on modern quantum processors. OmniQEC formulates QEC design as an iterative discovery process in which an orchestrator, implemented by advanced large language models (LLMs), coordinates code generation, code-level screening, syndrome-extraction synthesis, and decoder-based circuit evaluation. At its core, OmniQEC combines a self-evolving reasoning mechanism with a slow--fast synergistic workflow: a fast loop explores candidates using inexpensive code-level proxies, whereas a slow loop performs physically grounded circuit-level evaluation and feeds the resulting evidence back into the search. We evaluate OmniQEC across four qLDPC construction families, three LLM backends, and $14$ total-physical-qubit budgets per backend. The discovered codes show steadily improving logical-error suppression with increasing physical-qubit budgets and outperform the BB codes with $[\![72,12,6]\!]$ and $[\![144,12,12]\!]$ under complete-implementation budgets of 98 and 240 physical qubits, respectively. The discovered codes are hardware-friendly and may be of independent interest for practical QEC implementation. These findings pave the way towards LLM-assisted QEC discovery grounded in physically informed code--circuit--decoder co-design.
summary: The paper presents OmniQEC, a novel AI framework designed to discover practical Quantum Error-Correcting codes by simulating their performance on real quantum hardware. It employs a synergistic slow-fast loop where LLMs coordinate code generation and circuit evaluation. The results demonstrate that this physically informed approach yields superior error suppression compared to traditional methods.
main_problem: The challenge of discovering Quantum Error-Correcting (QEC) codes that are truly practical for deployment, as performance depends on the complex interplay between code structure, hardware constraints, syndrome extraction, and decoding.
main_result: OmniQEC discovers QEC codes that show steadily improving logical error suppression compared to standard reference codes when physical qubit budgets increase. The framework proves that circuit-level evaluation is superior to traditional code-level metrics for assessing practical performance.
method: The authors introduce OmniQEC, an AI scientist system orchestrated by LLMs that uses a slow–fast synergistic workflow. This combines fast, inexpensive code-level screening with a slow, physically grounded circuit-level evaluation loop.
model_or_system: The focus is on QEC codes, specifically evaluating qLDPC construction families, designed for implementation on modern quantum processors. The process models the full cycle from abstract code design to physical circuit execution and decoding.
key_observables: Logical Error Rate (LER) measured via $-\log_{10}(	ext{pLER})$, alongside code-level metrics like logical qubits ($k$), distance ($d$), and $\Phi_{code}$.
important_parameters: Total physical-qubit budget ($N$), qubit connectivity, and the specific LLM backend used for orchestration.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that an iterative, AI-guided search process can systematically navigate the vast design space to find hardware-friendly codes. A key limitation noted is the computational expense of the slow, circuit-level evaluation loop.

Figure 2 shows a performance frontier comparing discovered codes against reference codes based on LER vs. qubit budget. Figure 3/4 detail error suppression metrics and cost analysis.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the OmniQEC framework, detailing its LLM-orchestrated, dual-loop methodology (fast proxy search feeding into slow circuit simulation). It presents comparative results showing outperformance over benchmarks, validates the necessity of the full loop, and concludes with future directions for multi-agent system integration.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the gap between theoretical code design and physical implementation feasibility in quantum computing. The use of LLMs as an 'AI scientist' to guide complex scientific discovery is highly relevant to open quantum systems research that requires integrating multiple simulation/optimization modules.
